_comment: Binds each provider's account id to a canonical account. Copy to the path
named by OBDI_ACCOUNT_MAP and fill in with your own ids.
Find the provider account ids by running a pull: any unbound account is
reported in the output, because an unbound account still ingests but
Binding one account to two sources is the point. Where the routes agree
that is evidence the data is right; where they disagree the disagreement
is the finding; and either route surviving a consent expiry or an outage
This file names accounts, not balances. It is still yours - keep it with
_accounts_comment: DECLARED accounts - first-class registry entries that exist
independently of any data source. A mortgage without a feed and cash
in a tin are accounts; bindings below attach evidence to them, never
conjure them. The declared label wins the display name; opened/closed
drive the lifecycle import guard (rows outside the window must be
overridden); limits and rates are captured AHEAD of consumers - dated
windows with future dates welcome (a promotional rate carries the day
it reverts, which is what a future notification will hang from).

accounts.label: Piggy bank (no feed exists; manual entries only)

bindings.label: Starling personal current account, first-party API
The same account via the aggregator, for cross-checking

_actual_comment: Where each canonical account goes in Actual Budget, used by `obdi replay`.
The same question as above, asked in the opposite direction.
An account with no binding here is NOT replayed, and is named in the
command's output - a budget quietly missing an account looks like missing
spending, which is very hard to spot.
